title: A tort is a civil wrong, independent of contract, for which the common law ordinarily provides a civil remedy.

content.overview: A tort is a civil wrong, independent of contract, for which the common law ordinarily provides a civil remedy.
content.glance: A tort is a civil wrong, independent of contract, for which the common law ordinarily provides a civil remedy.
content.study: A tort is a civil wrong, independent of contract, for which the common law ordinarily provides a civil remedy.\n\nTort law is principally judge-made in India. The classical distinction is between duties imposed by law and duties voluntarily assumed by contract. The maxim ubi jus ibi remedium captures the remedial orientation, but the claimant must still identify a recognised cause of action. Tort may overlap with crime or breach of statutory duty without becoming identical to either.

sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: Tort law is principally judge-made in India. The classical distinction is between duties imposed by law and duties voluntarily assumed by contract. The maxim ubi jus ibi remedium captures the remedial orientation, but the claimant must still identify a recognised cause of action. Tort may overlap with crime or breach of statutory duty without becoming identical to either.

sections.heading: Textual Anatomy, Provisos & Statutory Deconstruction
sections.body: There is no single Indian Tort Act codifying the field. The applicable rule depends on the particular tort, precedent and any special statute. Consumer Protection Act 2019 and Motor Vehicles Act 1988 create specialised regimes that overlap with tort principles but do not codify all torts.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body: 1. A legally protected interest exists. 2. A legal duty is owed. 3. The duty is breached. 4. The breach causes legally attributable harm. 5. Damage is not too remote. 6. No complete defence defeats the claim.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: The claimant ordinarily bears the civil burden on the balance of probabilities. BSA 2023 governs applicable evidentiary questions but does not change substantive tort ingredients. The exact evidentiary burden varies with the tort.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: Ordinary tort claims are generally civil suits subject to CPC jurisdiction and the Limitation Act 1963 or a special statute. Plead the cause of action, duty, breach, causation, damage and relief.

examples.title: Illustration 1 — Doctrine Satisfied
examples.body: A claimant establishes duty, breach, causation and damage; absence of contract does not prevent a tort claim. The claimant must still prove the remaining ingredients on the civil standard.

examples.title: Illustration 2 — Boundary Defect
examples.body: Civil wrong is a broader category; breach of contract and breach of trust are civil wrongs without being torts. A court should not infer liability from the label alone.
